LLC ARTICLES OF ORGANIZATION
Prepared for Acme Ventures, LLC

ARTICLES OF ORGANIZATION DECLARATION
The name of the limited liability company is Acme Ventures, LLC. The purpose of Acme Ventures, LLC is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which a limited liability company may be organized under the California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act. Acme Ventures, LLC will be member-managed.

FORMATION BY FILING
Acme Ventures, LLC comes into existence as a California limited liability company on the date the California Secretary of State files its articles of organization — not on the date any operating agreement is signed, and not on the date the business starts operating. Before that filing is accepted, Acme Ventures, LLC has no legal existence as an LLC.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the Secretary of State for filing articles of organization on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, formation by organizers filing articles of organization (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.01.)
  "A limited liability company is formed when the Secretary of State has filed the articles of organization."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(d), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, the moment of formation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.01.)
  "Except in a proceeding by this state to dissolve a limited liability company, the filing of the articles of organization by the Secretary of State is conclusive proof that the organizer satisfied all conditions to the formation of a limited liability company."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(e), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, filing as conclusive proof of formation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.01.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, cited here to show that formation-by-filing (rather than formation-by-agreement) is how one real state actually structures LLC creation — not a claim about which state's law governs any particular company; LLC formation mechanics vary by state. All three quotes below come from subsections of the same statutory section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01, so they are treated as one source, not three independent ones. One thing this research could not verify: California's general corporation-filing statute (Cal. Corp. Code § 110) lets a corporation's filed instrument specify a delayed effective date up to 90 days out, but § 110 sits in the General Corporation Law (Title 1) and its delayed-effective-date language is written in terms of 'a corporation,' not an LLC. The current text of the LLC-specific formation statute, § 17702.01(d), states flatly that the LLC 'is formed when the Secretary of State has filed the articles of organization,' with no comparable 'or a later specified date' language found in this section or the surrounding LLC-formation article. Anyone relying on a delayed-effective-date option for an LLC filing should not assume one exists based on the corporation statute alone.

REQUIRED CONTENT OF THE ARTICLES OF ORGANIZATION
California's articles-of-organization statute requires the filed document to state: a lawful-purpose statement; the LLC's name (which must independently comply with the state's LLC-naming statute); the street address of the LLC's initial principal office, plus a separate mailing address if it differs; and the name and street address of the LLC's initial agent for service of process (address omitted if the agent is a registered corporate agent). Two further statements are required only if they apply — that the LLC will be manager-managed, or that it will be managed by a single manager — meaning the statute's default, absent either statement, is a member-managed LLC.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "The articles of organization shall state all of the following: (1) A statement that the purpose of the limited liability company is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which a limited liability company may be organized under this title. (2) The name of the limited liability company, which shall comply with Section 17701.08. (3) The street address of the initial principal office and the mailing address of the limited liability company if different from the street address of the initial principal office. (4) The name and street address of the initial agent for service of process of the limited liability company who meets the qualifications specified in subdivision (c) of Section 17701.13. If a corporate agent is designated, only the name of the agent shall be set forth. (5) If the limited liability company is to be manager-managed, the articles of organization shall contain a statement to that effect. (6) If the limited liability company is to be managed by only one manager, the articles of organization shall contain a statement to that effect."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(b), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, required content of the articles of organization (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.01.)
  Known gap: This is one state's list of required formation-document content, not a claim about what any other state's equivalent filing must contain — required content for an LLC's founding filing varies by state. This quote is drawn from Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(b), the same statutory section quoted in the sibling clause on when an LLC is formed; both clauses draw on subsections of one section, not two independent sources. This is a single statutory subsection (§ 17702.01(b)); no additional independent source was found for this.

THE LLC NAME REQUIREMENT
Under California's LLC-naming statute, an LLC's name must contain the words "limited liability company" or the abbreviation "LLC" or "L.L.C." (with "limited" shortenable to "Ltd." and "company" to "Co."). The same statute bars an LLC's name from including the words "bank," "trust," "trustee," "incorporated," "inc.," "corporation," or "corp.," and from including "insurer," "insurance company," or other words suggesting the business of issuing insurance policies.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "The name of a limited liability company shall contain the words "limited liability company," or the abbreviation "L.L.C." or "LLC." "Limited" may be abbreviated as "Ltd.," and "company" may be abbreviated as "Co.""
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.08(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, required name designator (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17701.08.)
  "The name shall not include the words "bank," "trust," "trustee," "incorporated," "inc.," "corporation," or "corp." and shall not include the words "insurer" or "insurance company" or any other words suggesting that it is in the business of issuing policies of insurance and assuming insurance risks."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.08(e), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, restricted words in an LLC name (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17701.08.)
  Known gap: This is one state's naming statute, not a claim about naming rules in any other state — restricted words and required designators for an LLC name vary by state. Both quotes below come from subsections of the same statutory section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.08, so they are one source, not two. One correction worth flagging: a commonly repeated assumption is that words like "city" are on this restricted list alongside "bank" and "corporation." The current, verified text of § 17701.08(e) does not include "city" or any municipal-sounding term among the restricted words — the restricted list here is limited to the banking/trust/insurance/corporate terms quoted above. This section also separately requires (in a subsection not quoted here, § 17701.08(b)) that a name be distinguishable in the Secretary of State's records from other registered entity names and not be likely to mislead the public, which is a separate, discretionary determination made by the Secretary of State rather than a fixed word list.

AGENT FOR SERVICE OF PROCESS DESIGNATION
The name of Acme Ventures, LLC's initial agent for service of process in California is Jordan Lee. The agent's street address in California is 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814.

AGENT FOR SERVICE OF PROCESS
California requires every LLC to continuously maintain, within the state, both an office and an agent for service of process. That agent must be either an individual who resides in California or a corporation qualified under state law to act as a registered corporate agent (in which case only the agent's name, not its address, is stated in the filing). If a designated agent resigns without being replaced, or cannot be located with reasonable diligence at its listed address, a court may order that the LLC instead be served by delivering process to the Secretary of State's office, with service deemed complete ten days after that delivery.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "A limited liability company shall designate and continuously maintain in this state both of the following: (1) An office, which need not be a place of its activity in this state. (2) An agent for service of process."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.13(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, duty to maintain an office and agent (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17701.13.)
  "An agent for service of process of a limited liability company or foreign limited liability company shall be an individual who is a resident of this state or a corporation that has complied with Section 1505 and whose capacity to act as an agent has not terminated. If a limited liability company or foreign limited liability company designates a corporation as its agent for service of process in an instrument filed with the Secretary of State, no address for that agent for service of process shall be set forth in that instrument."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.13(c), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, who may serve as agent for service of process (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17701.13.)
  "If an agent for service of process has resigned and has not been replaced or if the designated agent cannot with reasonable diligence be found at the address designated for personal delivery of the process, and it is shown by affidavit to the satisfaction of the court that process against a limited liability company or foreign limited liability company cannot be served with reasonable diligence upon the designated agent by hand in the manner provided in Section 415.10, subdivision (a) of Section 415.20, or subdivision (a) of Section 415.30 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may make an order that the service shall be made upon a domestic limited liability company or upon a registered foreign limited liability company by delivering by hand to the Secretary of State, or to any person employed in the Secretary of State's office in the capacity of assistant or deputy, one copy of the process for each defendant to be served, together with a copy of the order authorizing the service. Service in this manner shall be deemed complete on the 10th day after delivery of the process to the Secretary of State."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.16(c), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, service on the Secretary of State when the agent cannot be found (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17701.16.)
  Known gap: This is one state's agent-for-service-of-process requirement, not a claim about what any other state requires — whether an LLC must maintain an in-state agent at all, and who may serve as one, varies by state. The first two quotes come from subsections of the same section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.13, and are treated as one source; the third quote, describing what happens when no agent can be found, comes from a separate section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17701.16, and is an independently verified source.

THE FOLLOW-UP STATEMENT OF INFORMATION
Filing articles of organization does not end an LLC's filing obligations to the state. California requires every LLC to file an initial statement of information with the Secretary of State within 90 days after its articles of organization are filed, and then again every two years during the LLC's assigned filing period thereafter (or, if nothing has changed, to certify that no changes have occurred in lieu of refiling). The statement must report the LLC's name and Secretary of State file number, the name and street address of its current agent for service of process, its principal and mailing office addresses, the names and addresses of its managers (or, if it has none, its members), the general type of business it conducts, and a disclosure of whether any manager or member has an outstanding, non-appealable wage-order or Labor Code judgment against them.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Every limited liability company and every foreign limited liability company registered to transact intrastate business in this state shall deliver to the Secretary of State for filing within 90 days after the filing of its original articles of organization or registering to transact intrastate business and biennially thereafter during the applicable filing period, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, a statement of information containing: (1) The name of the limited liability company and the Secretary of State's file number... (2) The name and street address of the agent in this state for service of process required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13. If a corporate agent is designated, only the name of the agent shall be set forth. (3) The street address of its principal office... (4) The mailing address of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, if different from the street address of its principal office... (5) The name and complete business or residence addresses of any manager or managers and the chief executive officer, if any, appointed or elected in accordance with the articles of organization or operating agreement or, if no manager has been so elected or appointed, the name and business or residence address of each member. (6) If the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company chooses to receive renewal notices and any other notifications from the Secretary of State by electronic mail instead of by United States mail, the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company shall include a valid electronic mail address... (7) The general type of business that constitutes the principal business activity of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, such as, for example, manufacturer of aircraft, wholesale liquor distributor, or retail department store. (8) ...a statement indicating whether any manager [or member] has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code..."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, initial and biennial statement of information (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)
  "For purposes of this section, the applicable filing period for a limited liability company shall be the calendar month during which its original articles of organization was filed or, in the case of a foreign limited liability company, the month during which its application for registration was filed, and the immediately preceding five calendar months. The Secretary of State shall provide a notice to each limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to comply with this section approximately three months prior to the close of the applicable filing period... The failure of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to receive the notice shall not exempt the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company from complying with this section."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(c), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, how the two-year filing period is measured (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)
  Known gap: This is one state's periodic-reporting requirement for LLCs, not a claim about what any other state requires after formation — whether a follow-up report is required at all, and how often, varies by state. Both quotes below are subsections of the same statutory section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09, and are treated as one source. This section notes it became operative in 2022 (or earlier upon a state IT-system certification); it has since been amended again, most recently effective January 1, 2023, so its current text is what is quoted here.

THE ANNUAL LLC TAX
Filing articles of organization also triggers a state tax obligation separate from the Secretary of State's filing fee. California's Revenue and Taxation Code requires every LLC doing business in the state — and, independently, every LLC whose articles of organization have been accepted by the Secretary of State, whether or not it is yet doing business — to pay an annual tax in the amount set as the state's minimum franchise tax, currently eight hundred dollars ($800), due by the 15th day of the fourth month of the taxable year. That obligation continues for each taxable year, or part of one, until a certificate of dissolution or cancellation is filed with the Secretary of State.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Except as provided in subdivision (g), for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1997, a limited liability company doing business in this state (as defined in Section 23101) shall pay annually to this state a tax for the privilege of doing business in this state in an amount equal to the applicable amount specified in subdivision (d) of Section 23153 for the taxable year."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941(a), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the annual tax for doing business in the state (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17941.)
  "In addition to any limited liability company that is doing business in this state and is therefore subject to the tax imposed by subdivision (a), for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1997, a limited liability company shall pay annually the tax prescribed in subdivision (a) if articles of organization have been accepted, or a certificate of registration has been issued, by the office of the Secretary of State. The tax shall be paid for each taxable year, or part thereof, until a certificate of cancellation of registration or of articles of organization is filed on behalf of the limited liability company with the office of the Secretary of State. ... Every limited liability company doing business in this state as described in subdivision (a) that organizes or registers with the Secretary of the State pursuant to subdivision (b) on or after January 1, 2021, and before January 1, 2024, shall not be subject to the tax imposed under this section for its first taxable year."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941(b)(1) & (g), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the tax on filing (independent of doing business) and the now-expired 2021-2023 first-year exemption (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17941.)
  "Except as provided in paragraph (2), paragraph (1) of subdivision (f) of Section 23151, paragraph (1) of subdivision (f) of Section 23181, and paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 23183, corporations subject to the minimum franchise tax shall pay annually to the state a minimum franchise tax of eight hundred dollars ($800)."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23153(d)(1), The Corporation Franchise Tax, the $800 minimum franchise tax amount cross-referenced for LLCs (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23153.)
  Known gap: This is one state's minimum annual LLC tax, not a claim about what any other state charges — whether a state imposes a flat annual LLC tax at all, and in what amount, varies by state. The first two quotes below are subsections of the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941, and are one source; the $800 dollar figure itself is set in a separate section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23153(d)(1) (written for corporations generally but cross-referenced by § 17941(a) to set the LLC tax amount), and is an independently verified source. On the first-year exemption specifically: a temporary waiver did exist, but it applied only to LLCs that organized or registered with the Secretary of State on or after January 1, 2021 and before January 1, 2024 — that window has closed, so an LLC newly formed today would not fall within it. Separately, and more recently, the same statute (as amended by Stats. 2026, Ch. 85 (SB 180), effective July 13, 2026) now provides that for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027 and before January 1, 2030, LLCs required to file a return under a specific cross-referenced provision (Rev. & Tax. Code § 18633.5) pay a reduced $400 tax for their first taxable year instead of the full $800 — a different, narrower provision than the earlier 2021-2023 exemption, tied to taxable years beginning in 2027-2029 rather than to a company's formation date, and not yet operative as of this verification date. This research did not independently trace § 18633.5 to confirm exactly which LLCs that reduced-rate provision reaches.

ORGANIZER SIGNATURE
Executed by the organizer:

Organizer: Jordan Lee

Signature: ☐ _________________________ Date: _______________

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THIS DOCUMENT
File an initial Statement of Information
California requires every LLC to file an initial statement of information with the Secretary of State within 90 days after its articles of organization are filed, then again every two years during the LLC's assigned filing period. This project's own Statement of Information document covers that filing.
[checked 2026-09-02]
  Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, initial and biennial statement of information (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)
Statement of Information due: not shown — "Date articles were filed (if already filed)" wasn't entered above.

Pay California's $800 annual LLC tax
Beyond the Secretary of State's filing fee, California's Revenue and Taxation Code requires every LLC whose articles of organization have been accepted by the Secretary of State to pay an annual tax equal to the state's minimum franchise tax, currently $800, due by the 15th day of the fourth month of the LLC's taxable year. This project doesn't collect enough information to compute that date reliably -- it depends on the LLC's own taxable year, not simply its filing date -- so no reminder is offered for it here.
[checked 2026-09-01]
  Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941(a), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the annual tax for doing business in the state (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17941.)
  Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23153(d)(1), The Corporation Franchise Tax, the $800 minimum franchise tax amount cross-referenced for LLCs (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23153.)

expectedJSON.body: Filing articles of organization does not end an LLC's filing obligations to the state. California requires every LLC to file an initial statement of information with the Secretary of State within 90 days after its articles of organization are filed, and then again every two years during the LLC's assigned filing period thereafter (or, if nothing has changed, to certify that no changes have occurred in lieu of refiling). The statement must report the LLC's name and Secretary of State file number, the name and street address of its current agent for service of process, its principal and mailing office addresses, the names and addresses of its managers (or, if it has none, its members), the general type of business it conducts, and a disclosure of whether any manager or member has an outstanding, non-appealable wage-order or Labor Code judgment against them.

citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, initial and biennial statement of information
citations.quote: Every limited liability company and every foreign limited liability company registered to transact intrastate business in this state shall deliver to the Secretary of State for filing within 90 days after the filing of its original articles of organization or registering to transact intrastate business and biennially thereafter during the applicable filing period, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, a statement of information containing: (1) The name of the limited liability company and the Secretary of State's file number... (2) The name and street address of the agent in this state for service of process required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13. If a corporate agent is designated, only the name of the agent shall be set forth. (3) The street address of its principal office... (4) The mailing address of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, if different from the street address of its principal office... (5) The name and complete business or residence addresses of any manager or managers and the chief executive officer, if any, appointed or elected in accordance with the articles of organization or operating agreement or, if no manager has been so elected or appointed, the name and business or residence address of each member. (6) If the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company chooses to receive renewal notices and any other notifications from the Secretary of State by electronic mail instead of by United States mail, the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company shall include a valid electronic mail address... (7) The general type of business that constitutes the principal business activity of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, such as, for example, manufacturer of aircraft, wholesale liquor distributor, or retail department store. (8) ...a statement indicating whether any manager [or member] has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code...

citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, how the two-year filing period is measured
citations.quote: For purposes of this section, the applicable filing period for a limited liability company shall be the calendar month during which its original articles of organization was filed or, in the case of a foreign limited liability company, the month during which its application for registration was filed, and the immediately preceding five calendar months. The Secretary of State shall provide a notice to each limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to comply with this section approximately three months prior to the close of the applicable filing period... The failure of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to receive the notice shall not exempt the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company from complying with this section.

expectedJSON.gap: This is one state's periodic-reporting requirement for LLCs, not a claim about what any other state requires after formation — whether a follow-up report is required at all, and how often, varies by state. Both quotes below are subsections of the same statutory section, Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09, and are treated as one source. This section notes it became operative in 2022 (or earlier upon a state IT-system certification); it has since been amended again, most recently effective January 1, 2023, so its current text is what is quoted here.

expectedJSON.body: Filing articles of organization also triggers a state tax obligation separate from the Secretary of State's filing fee. California's Revenue and Taxation Code requires every LLC doing business in the state — and, independently, every LLC whose articles of organization have been accepted by the Secretary of State, whether or not it is yet doing business — to pay an annual tax in the amount set as the state's minimum franchise tax, currently eight hundred dollars ($800), due by the 15th day of the fourth month of the taxable year. That obligation continues for each taxable year, or part of one, until a certificate of dissolution or cancellation is filed with the Secretary of State.

citations.cite: Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the annual tax for doing business in the state
citations.quote: Except as provided in subdivision (g), for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1997, a limited liability company doing business in this state (as defined in Section 23101) shall pay annually to this state a tax for the privilege of doing business in this state in an amount equal to the applicable amount specified in subdivision (d) of Section 23153 for the taxable year.

citations.cite: Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the tax on filing (independent of doing business) and the now-expired 2021-2023 first-year exemption
citations.quote: In addition to any limited liability company that is doing business in this state and is therefore subject to the tax imposed by subdivision (a), for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1997, a limited liability company shall pay annually the tax prescribed in subdivision (a) if articles of organization have been accepted, or a certificate of registration has been issued, by the office of the Secretary of State. The tax shall be paid for each taxable year, or part thereof, until a certificate of cancellation of registration or of articles of organization is filed on behalf of the limited liability company with the office of the Secretary of State. ... Every limited liability company doing business in this state as described in subdivision (a) that organizes or registers with the Secretary of the State pursuant to subdivision (b) on or after January 1, 2021, and before January 1, 2024, shall not be subject to the tax imposed under this section for its first taxable year.

citations.cite: The Corporation Franchise Tax, the $800 minimum franchise tax amount cross-referenced for LLCs
citations.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (2), paragraph (1) of subdivision (f) of Section 23151, paragraph (1) of subdivision (f) of Section 23181, and paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 23183, corporations subject to the minimum franchise tax shall pay annually to the state a minimum franchise tax of eight hundred dollars ($800).

expectedJSON.gap: This is one state's minimum annual LLC tax, not a claim about what any other state charges — whether a state imposes a flat annual LLC tax at all, and in what amount, varies by state. The first two quotes below are subsections of the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941, and are one source; the $800 dollar figure itself is set in a separate section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23153(d)(1) (written for corporations generally but cross-referenced by § 17941(a) to set the LLC tax amount), and is an independently verified source. On the first-year exemption specifically: a temporary waiver did exist, but it applied only to LLCs that organized or registered with the Secretary of State on or after January 1, 2021 and before January 1, 2024 — that window has closed, so an LLC newly formed today would not fall within it. Separately, and more recently, the same statute (as amended by Stats. 2026, Ch. 85 (SB 180), effective July 13, 2026) now provides that for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027 and before January 1, 2030, LLCs required to file a return under a specific cross-referenced provision (Rev. & Tax. Code § 18633.5) pay a reduced $400 tax for their first taxable year instead of the full $800 — a different, narrower provision than the earlier 2021-2023 exemption, tied to taxable years beginning in 2027-2029 rather than to a company's formation date, and not yet operative as of this verification date. This research did not independently trace § 18633.5 to confirm exactly which LLCs that reduced-rate provision reaches.
